title: Positive-degree constant cohomology vanishes on closed subschemes of the spectrum of a normal domain with separably closed fraction field (Stacks 09ZC)
statement: Let $R$ be a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] whose field of fractions is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed], and let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] (a closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$). Then for every finite abelian group $M$, with constant sheaf $\underline M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $Z_{\Et}$, and every integer $q\ge1$, the etale cohomology group [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] $H^q(Z_{\Et},\underline M)$ is zero.

source.place: Lemma 09ZC (label lemma-gabber-for-absolutely-algebraically-closed), line 14445, and its proof; Stacks' hypothesis 'normal integral affine scheme with separably closed function field' is Spec of a normal domain with separably closed fraction field

proof.text: Use Mathlib IsClosedImmersion.Spec_iff to choose I and an isomorphism e : Z to Spec(R/I). The theorem requires no change to its signature.
gabber_quotient_localizations supplies strict henselianity at every prime of R/I. Its proof uses the ring-level 09Z9 theorems and the already stated strictly henselian quotient theorem.

Let F be the constant sheaf with value M on Spec(R/I). gabber_quotient_principal_h1 implies every element x of H-one on D(f+g) is zero by Subsingleton.elim. Therefore the kernel implication required by gabberCriterion holds, independently of its two restriction-zero premises.
Apply Etale.gabberCriterion to R/I, F, and the preceding hypotheses. The positive integer q has q.toNat positive, so the criterion gives Subsingleton (Sheaf.H F q.toNat).

Use isZero_constant_cohomology_iff_subsingleton_H_of_iso with e to transfer that vanishing to derived constant cohomology on Z. The equality of the integer cast of q.toNat with q follows from q >= 1, completing the original goal.

split_report.summary: Split along the proof of Stacks 09ZC in five steps: (1) Z is isomorphic over X to Spec(R/I) (affine form of closed immersion) and etale cohomology with constant coefficients is transported along the isomorphism (written out); (2) local rings of R are strictly henselian by 09Z9 = sbc-lem-etale-over-normal (2), using the new Mathlib leaves lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field (stalks of Spec R are R_p, function field is Frac R) and lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain (00GY with the fraction field clause); (3) local rings R'_p' = R_p/IR_p are strictly henselian by the new node lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-quotient (05WS for a strictly henselian ring); (4) for h in R' with a lift f: f = 0 gives D(h) empty, otherwise R_f is a normal domain with fraction field K, R'_h = R_f/IR_f is a closed subscheme of Spec R_f, and the new node lem-weil-pbc-gabber-h1-absolutely-algebraically-closed (09ZB) gives H^1(D(h), M) = 0 (D(h) = Spec R'_h by the open immersion leaf, restriction of the constant sheaf constant by lemma-constructible-pullback-constant); (5) the new node lem-weil-pbc-gabber-criterion (0GY0) concludes since the source of the Mayer-Vietoris H^1 map is already 0. 09ZA is used only inside the proof of 09ZB and is not created here. The statement is kept.
